title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Implementation Opinions on the Selection, Training, and Assessment of People's Jurors
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court  Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the Implementation Opinions on the Work of Selection, Training, and Assessment of People's Assessors

Fa Fa [2004] No. 22

High People's Courts and Judicial Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; Production and Construction Corps Judicial Bureau of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Implementation Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice on the Work of Selection, Training, and Assessment of People's Assessors are hereby issued to you for your earnest study, implementation, and execution. If problems arise during implementation, please promptly report them to the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice.

December 13, 2004

Supreme People's Court  Ministry of Justice

Implementation Opinions on the Work of Selection, Training, and Assessment of People's Assessors

In order to correctly implement the relevant provisions of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Improving the System of People's Assessors (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision") and to ensure the smooth progress of the work of selecting, training, and assessing people's assessors, these Implementation Opinions are formulated.

Article 1. Pursuant to Articles 8, 15, 16, and 17 of the Decision, the work of selecting, training, and assessing people's assessors shall be carried out by the basic people's court jointly with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level.

Article 2. Pursuant to Paragraph 2 of Article 4 of the Decision, a citizen serving as a people's assessor shall generally have an educational level of associate degree or above. For localities where the implementation of this provision is genuinely difficult, and for citizens who are older or have high prestige among the masses, the educational requirements for serving as a people's assessor may be appropriately relaxed.

Article 3. Taking into account factors such as the number of cases in its jurisdiction, population size, geographical area, ethnic composition, and the needs of higher-level people's courts to randomly select people's assessors from the basic people's court, the basic people's court shall propose opinions on the number of people's assessors for its own court and submit them to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level for determination.

Article 4. The selection of people's assessors shall adhere to the principles of fairness, impartiality, and openness.

Article 5. The basic people's court shall, one month before the commencement of the selection of people's assessors, make a public announcement to the community regarding the number of people's assessors to be selected, the selection conditions, procedures, and other relevant matters.

Article 6. A citizen who meets the conditions to serve as a people's assessor may be recommended in writing to the local basic people's court by the organization to which he belongs, or by the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence, with his consent. Alternatively, he may submit a written application to the basic people's court at his registered domicile or habitual residence.

Article 7. For citizens recommended or applying to serve as people's assessors, the basic people's court shall conduct a review in accordance with Articles 4, 5, and 6 of the Decision. After preliminarily determining candidates for people's assessors, the court shall send the list of candidates and relevant materials to the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level for comments. When necessary, the basic people's court, jointly with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level, shall conduct investigations at the organization to which the citizen belongs, or at the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence.

Article 8. Based on the review results and the number of people's assessors for its court, the basic people's court shall determine the candidates for people's assessors, and the president of the court shall submit them to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level for appointment.

When determining the candidates for people's assessors, attention shall be paid to including persons from all social strata in order to reflect the broad representation of the source of people's assessors.

A citizen may not serve as a people's assessor in two or more basic people's courts simultaneously.

Article 9. The basic people's court shall notify the people's assessor, his organization, and the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence in writing of the appointment decision, and send a copy of the appointment list to the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level, and at the same time make a public announcement to the community.

Article 10. After being appointed and before lawfully participating in the trial activities of the people's court, a people's assessor must undergo training.

Article 11. The basic people's court shall formulate a training plan for people's assessors based on the actual circumstances of its trial work. After soliciting comments from the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level, the training shall be specifically carried out by the judicial personnel training institution of the people's court.

Article 12. Training provided to people's assessors shall meet the actual needs of their participation in trial activities. The training content shall include basic legal knowledge, basic rules of trial work, trial professional ethics, and trial discipline.

Article 13. The judicial personnel training institution of the people's court that undertakes the training of people's assessors shall notify the people's assessor in writing seven days in advance to attend the training, and at the same time notify the people's assessor's organization and the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence in writing, so that the people's assessor himself, his organization, and the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence can arrange work and daily life to ensure that the people's assessor attends the training on time.

Article 14. Expenses such as transportation and meals incurred by a people's assessor for participating in training shall be subsidized by the basic people's court to which he is attached, with reference to the local travel expense payment standards.

During the period when a people's assessor who is employed participates in training, his organization shall not deduct or covertly deduct his wages, bonuses, or other fringe benefits.

For a people's assessor with no fixed income during the period of participating in training, the basic people's court to which he is attached shall provide a subsidy based on the actual number of training days, with reference to the local average monthly money wage level of employees in the previous year.

Article 15. The basic people's court shall formulate assessment methods for people's assessors in the performance of their duties after soliciting comments from the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level. The assessment content includes the actual performance of jury duties, ideological character, work attitude, trial discipline, and trial style, among others.

Where an intermediate people's court or a high people's court randomly selects people's assessors from the roster of the basic people's court in its locality to participate in the trial work of its own court, it shall notify the basic people's court to which the people's assessor is attached of the circumstances of the people's assessor's performance of duties in its court, which shall serve as one of the bases for assessing the people's assessor.

Article 16. For people's assessors who have achieved significant results or have other outstanding deeds in trial work, the basic people's court, jointly with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level, shall give commendations and rewards, and the basic people's court shall promptly notify in writing the people's assessor himself, his organization, and the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence.

Article 17. Where a people's assessor falls under any of the circumstances listed in Article 17 of the Decision, the basic people's court, jointly with the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level, shall investigate and verify. If the facts are verified, the president of the basic people's court shall submit to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level a request to remove the person from the position of people's assessor.

For a people's assessor who commits an act listed in Article 17, Paragraph (4) of the Decision that does not yet constitute a crime, in addition to removing him from the position of people's assessor in accordance with the law, the basic people's court may, when necessary, recommend in writing to his organization that disciplinary action be taken against him in accordance with relevant provisions.

Article 18. The term of office of a people's assessor is five years, and vacancies shall be filled by supplementary selection in accordance with the statutory procedures. After the term of office of a people's assessor expires, the position of people's assessor is automatically terminated.

Article 19. For the removal of a people's assessor from office in accordance with Articles 17 and 18 of these Implementation Opinions, the basic people's court shall notify the removed person, his organization, and the grassroots organization at his registered domicile or habitual residence in writing of the removal decision, and send a copy of the removal list to the judicial administrative organ of the people's government at the same level, and at the same time make a public announcement to the community.

Article 20. Expenses such as transportation and meals incurred by a people's assessor for participating in trial activities shall be subsidized by the people's court with reference to the local travel expense payment standards.

Where an intermediate people's court or a high people's court randomly selects people's assessors from the roster of the basic people's court in its locality to participate in the collegiate bench trial of its own court, it shall provide various subsidies to the people's assessor in accordance with Article 18 of the Decision and the preceding paragraph.

Article 21. Where an employed people's assessor has his wages, bonuses, or other fringe benefits deducted or covertly deducted by his organization due to his participation in training or trial activities, the basic people's court shall issue corrective opinions to his organization or the competent authority at a higher level of his organization.

Article 22. People's courts and judicial administrative organs at all levels shall incorporate the necessary expenditures for implementing the people's assessor system into the annual budget for operational expenses and timely declare them to the financial department of the people's government at the same level, in order to secure funding from the government finance at the same level.

People's courts and judicial administrative organs at all levels shall separately allocate, separately manage, and ensure dedicated use of all funds for the implementation of the people's assessor system, so as to guarantee the effective implementation of the people's assessor system.

Article 23. The interpretation of these Implementation Opinions shall be jointly the responsibility of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice.

Article 24. These Implementation Opinions shall come into effect as of the date of promulgation.
